:::{#cor-weibull-hazard-monotone}
#### The Weibull shape sets the direction of the hazard

If $T$ has the [Weibull distribution](#def-weibull) with shape $\shape$ and rate $\rate$,
then on $t > 0$ its hazard $\h(t)$ is:

- strictly increasing if $\shape > 1$
- constant if $\shape = 1$
- strictly decreasing if $\shape < 1$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-weibull, $\h(t) = \shape\rate t^{\shape-1}$ for $t > 0$, so:

$$
\ba
\frac{d}{dt}\h(t)
&= \frac{d}{dt} \shape\rate t^{\shape-1}
&& (\text{Weibull hazard}) \\
&= \shape(\shape - 1)\rate t^{\shape-2}
&& (\text{power rule})
\ea
$$

For $t > 0$, the factors $\shape$, $\rate$, and $t^{\shape-2}$ are all positive,
so $\frac{d}{dt}\h(t)$ has the sign of $\shape - 1$:
positive for $\shape > 1$, zero for $\shape = 1$, and negative for $\shape < 1$.
A function with a positive (negative) derivative on an interval
is strictly increasing (decreasing) there,
and one with a zero derivative is constant.

:::
